A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WeatherWeaver and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing material can be matched reliably across the appendix additions and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original weather-synthesis and removal evaluations, human and VLM preference results in Tables 2–3, and qualitative ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative rain-removal comparisons in Fig. S7.

M1.justification: The complementary synthesis/removal models, six-component conditioning, denoising objectives, and staged training procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A clarifies existing weather-strength controls without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same three training-data sources and Waymo, DL3DV, and Pexels evaluation coverage. The added outdoor rain-removal examples remain within the existing task and domain.

E2.justification: New Fig. S7 evaluates Rain-LHP and RainMamba against WeatherWeaver on three rain-removal examples. These comparators were absent from v1; the comparator sets in the existing quantitative evaluations remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported 40 synthesis and 55 removal videos, metrics, synthesis strength of 1.0, and training settings are unchanged. The newly documented strength normalization is additional implementation information; no revised protocol is stated.

E4.justification: The architecture/data-source ablations, strength-control and temporal demonstrations, downstream perception example, and failure cases are retained. New Fig. S7 expands ordinary qualitative baseline comparisons without adding a distinct diagnostic or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repeated human studies with standard deviations, 11 users per comparison, and seven differently seeded VLM evaluations. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: v2 adds qualitative outputs for Rain-LHP, RainMamba, and WeatherWeaver in Fig. S7 and replaces WeatherWeaver's parking-lot rain-removal output in Fig. 4. Tables 1–3 retain identical numerical entries; the image replacement does not establish a measured performance gain.

T1.justification: The latent-space definitions, six-component weather representation, and objectives (1)–(2) are unchanged. Appendix A provides physical descriptions and normalization details, without new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about controllable weather synthesis/removal, complementary models, mixed-source data, and superiority over existing methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations of baseline performance and data-source contributions are unchanged. Limitations concerning fine details, nighttime videos, and short offline video processing remain, including the appendix failure discussion moved across pages.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly explains the Unreal Engine quantities underlying each strength control and normalization to [0, 1]. v2 also supplies a clickable project-website link where v1 only mentions the website; this does not establish a code or data release.

R1.justification: v2 adds Guo et al.'s real-rain-removal work and Wu et al.'s RainMamba as references supporting Fig. S7. The existing related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix A gains Training Details and Weather Strength Definition subheadings and a short explanatory paragraph. Other changes are limited wording and cross-reference edits; the main narrative and section organization are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-example Fig. S7, replaces one displayed output in Fig. 4, and redistributes existing appendix figures. v1's synthesis and failure figures S7–S8 become S8–S9; the quantitative table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves documentation of the central weather-strength controls and adds relevant qualitative comparisons with two rain-removal methods. These provide clearer implementation guidance and modest additional empirical support. The unchanged quantitative evidence and qualitative-only scope of the new comparisons limit the overall gain.
